Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
hey, can you turn these notes into a draft volunteer transport rota for North Quay Neighbors for the week of June 10 through June 14? We coordinate rides for people who cannot reliably get to appointments or essential errands on their own. This is only a working draft for the volunteer coordinator to review, not a confirmed schedule. Please use the requests and availability below; some details are still unsettled, so make that visible instead of quietly filling gaps. The group usually sends the rota by email on Friday afternoon, but this one is needed for a Thursday evening check-in, and the coordinator wants to see where coverage is thin before then.

There are six ride requests so far. On Monday, June 10, Ms. Inez Calder needs a ride from 18 Alder Court to the Riverbend clinic for a 9:20 a.m. appointment; she asked to be picked up at 8:35 and expects to be ready to return around 10:45. She uses a folding walker that fits in a regular trunk, and can manage two steps with an arm for support. On Tuesday, June 11, Tomas Venn needs a trip from 4 Lark Street to the market on Cedar Avenue, with pickup at 11:00 a.m. and a return pickup at 12:15. He has two reusable bags, no mobility equipment, and said, “I can wait inside if the driver is a few minutes late.” On Wednesday, June 12, Priya Nair has a 1:30 p.m. eye appointment at the Eastgate Health Centre, leaving from 72 Rowan Lane; she requested pickup at 12:45 and expects to leave the clinic at 3:00. She does not need help getting into the car, but she has asked for a driver to wait nearby rather than make a second trip.

On Thursday, June 13, a request from Leon Park is pencilled in for a ride from 9 Quarry Walk to the Riverbend clinic. The appointment is at 10:10 a.m., and he asked for pickup at 9:25, with an estimated return at 11:30. He needs the wheelchair-accessible van and a driver who is trained to secure a chair. The clinic has not yet confirmed his appointment: the coordinator is expecting a call on Wednesday. If the appointment is confirmed by Wednesday noon, reserve the accessible van for Leon; if it is not confirmed by then, leave that vehicle unassigned for the week and mark this ride as awaiting confirmation, not cancelled. On Friday, June 14, Mara Okafor needs a ride from 16 Finch Crescent to the library branch on Mill Road, pickup at 2:00 p.m. and return at 3:30. She uses a cane and says she can get in and out of a standard car. The sixth request is from Eli Moss for Friday, June 14: pickup at 8:10 a.m. at 31 Bell Mews, drop-off at the Cedar Street food pantry, and a return trip at 9:40. Eli has not said whether he needs any mobility assistance, so that still needs asking.

We have four volunteers who have shared their availability. Rosa Bell can drive Monday and Thursday, 8:00 a.m. to noon, and has a standard car with room for one passenger plus a folding walker. She is not trained on the accessible van. In a message she wrote, “Please don't put me down for anything after noon; I have another commitment.” Dev Shah is available Tuesday and Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., has a standard car, and is comfortable carrying grocery bags. He cannot work Wednesday. Kim Alvarez is available Monday through Wednesday, 12:00 to 5:00 p.m., has a standard car, and can wait during an appointment, but cannot do morning pickups. Jo Field is available Thursday and Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and is the only volunteer currently trained to drive and secure passengers in the accessible van. Jo also has a standard car available, but only one vehicle can be used at a time. No one has given availability beyond these dates or hours, and we have not checked whether volunteers can take two assignments in one day.

For vehicles, the group has Rosa's and Dev's standard cars, Kim's standard car, and Jo's standard car, plus one organization accessible van. The accessible van is not available for ordinary trips this week because a maintenance check is booked Friday morning. The mechanic expects it back by 1:00 p.m. Friday, but has not guaranteed that time; don't treat it as available for Mara's 2:00 p.m. ride unless the return is confirmed. This doesn't affect the possible Thursday reservation for Leon. We have no information about passenger capacity beyond the details above, so please don't assume two riders can share a trip. We also don't yet know whether any volunteer besides Jo can cover Leon if the appointment is confirmed.

one thing to keep in mind on the Wednesday call, if the clinic hasn't confirmed Leon's appointment by noon the accessible van should stay open and the coordinator should be told there is no confirmed driver or ride for him yet. If confirmation comes after noon, flag that as a late change for the coordinator to decide; don't silently switch the vehicle or claim that Jo has agreed to a different time. For Eli, leave the assistance question visible as unresolved rather than guessing from the short trip. The coordinator may be able to ask him during the Thursday check-in, but we don't know that yet. Include each ride request even where coverage is uncertain, and distinguish confirmed information from open questions.

please make the output a numbered checklist, not a table. For every proposed assignment, put the request or availability evidence first and the suggested assignment second, so the coordinator can check why it fits. Include a separate checklist item for each ride, and mark any ride with no supported assignment as uncovered or awaiting confirmation as appropriate. After the six ride items, include a short numbered section called “Questions and checks before sending” with the unresolved items and vehicle timing issue. Keep the actual pickup and return times, addresses, destinations, dates, and relevant mobility or vehicle details in the prompt result. Don't write a message to riders, don't decide whether a volunteer has accepted a shift, and don't make the draft sound approved. Finish with that questions-and-checks section; we need the open issues in front of the coordinator, not a general closing note.", "output": "Create a **working draft volunteer transport rota** for North Quay Neighbors for June 10–14. The rota is for the volunteer coordinator to review at a Thursday evening check-in; it is not a confirmed schedule. Use only the requests and availability below, show unsettled details as open questions, and identify thin coverage. The group usually emails its rota on Friday afternoon, but this draft is needed earlier.

Return the result as a **numbered checklist, not a table**. Include a separate item for each of the six ride requests. For every proposed assignment, list the request or availability evidence first, then the suggested assignment. Mark rides without a supported assignment as uncovered or awaiting confirmation, as appropriate. After the six ride items, add a numbered section titled **“Questions and checks before sending”** covering unresolved items and the vehicle timing issue. Keep the actual pickup and return times, addresses, destinations, dates, and relevant mobility or vehicle details. Do not write messages to riders, decide whether a volunteer has accepted a shift, or present the draft as approved. Finish with the questions-and-checks section, with no general closing note.

### Ride requests

- **Monday, June 10 — Inez Calder:** Pickup at 8:35 a.m. from 18 Alder Court to the Riverbend clinic for a 9:20 a.m. appointment; expected return around 10:45 a.m. She uses a folding walker that fits in a regular trunk and can manage two steps with an arm for support.
- **Tuesday, June 11 — Tomas Venn:** Pickup at 11:00 a.m. from 4 Lark Street to the market on Cedar Avenue, with a return pickup at 12:15 p.m. He has two reusable bags and no mobility equipment. He said, “I can wait inside if the driver is a few minutes late.”
- **Wednesday, June 12 — Priya Nair:** Pickup at 12:45 p.m. from 72 Rowan Lane for a 1:30 p.m. eye appointment at Eastgate Health Centre; she expects to leave at 3:00 p.m. She needs no help getting into the car and has requested that the driver wait nearby rather than make a second trip.
- **Thursday, June 13 — Leon Park:** Pencilled-in request from 9 Quarry Walk to the Riverbend clinic for a 10:10 a.m. appointment. Pickup requested at 9:25 a.m.; estimated return at 11:30 a.m. He needs the wheelchair-accessible van and a driver trained to secure a chair. The clinic has not confirmed the appointment; the coordinator expects a call Wednesday. **If confirmed by Wednesday noon, reserve the accessible van for Leon. If it is not confirmed by then, leave the vehicle unassigned for the week and mark the ride awaiting confirmation, not cancelled.** If confirmation comes after noon, flag it as a late change for the coordinator to decide; do not silently switch the vehicle or claim Jo has agreed to a different time.
- **Friday, June 14 — Mara Okafor:** Pickup at 2:00 p.m. from 16 Finch Crescent to the library branch on Mill Road, with return at 3:30 p.m. She uses a cane and says she can get in and out of a standard car.
- **Friday, June 14 — Eli Moss:** Pickup at 8:10 a.m. from 31 Bell Mews to the Cedar Street food pantry, with return at 9:40 a.m. He has not said whether he needs mobility assistance. Keep this question unresolved rather than guessing; the coordinator may be able to ask at the Thursday check-in, but that is not known.

### Volunteer availability

- **Rosa Bell:** Available Monday and Thursday, 8:00 a.m.–noon. Has a standard car with room for one passenger plus a folding walker; is not trained on the accessible van. She wrote, “Please don't put me down for anything after noon; I have another commitment.”
- **Dev Shah:** Available Tuesday and Friday, 8:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m. Has a standard car and is comfortable carrying grocery bags. Cannot work Wednesday.
- **Kim Alvarez:** Available Monday through Wednesday, noon–5:00 p.m. Has a standard car and can wait during an appointment, but cannot do morning pickups.
- **Jo Field:** Available Thursday and Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. Is the only volunteer currently trained to drive and secure passengers in the accessible van. Also has a standard car, but can use only one vehicle at a time.

No one has provided availability beyond these dates or hours, and it has not been checked whether volunteers can take two assignments in one day. Do not assume they can.

### Vehicle details and open checks

Available vehicles are Rosa’s, Dev’s, and Kim’s standard cars; Jo’s standard car; and one organization accessible van. The van is not available for ordinary trips this week because a maintenance check is booked for Friday morning. The mechanic expects it back by 1:00 p.m. Friday but has not guaranteed the time. Do not treat it as available for Mara’s 2:00 p.m. ride unless its return is confirmed. This maintenance check does not affect a possible Thursday reservation for Leon. No passenger capacity details are available beyond those stated above, so do not assume riders can share a trip. It is not known whether anyone besides Jo can cover Leon if the appointment is confirmed.

On Wednesday, if the clinic has not confirmed Leon’s appointment by noon, leave the accessible van open and tell the coordinator that Leon has no confirmed driver or ride yet. Include every request even when coverage is uncertain, and distinguish confirmed information from open questions. Do not fill in missing details or decide unresolved matters on the coordinator’s behalf."}]
